title: Interleaved latency vs fidelity handoff - INT8/FP8 workshop

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-08-05 11:30 PDT | Duration: 54 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samantha Lee; Carlos Mendez; Priya Nair; Dr. Anika Rao; Tom Bishop; Ravi Patel; Lena Morris

Summary (auto): Quick optimize console workshop — build precision profiles, show fidelity heatmaps, demo fallback rules, discuss pilot and security.

[00:00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samantha, AE at Redwood. With me is Carlos, our SE, and Priya from product.
[00:00:07] Dr. Anika: Hi, thanks. Quick background — Mediscribe is building triage summarization for clinical notes, some PHI in scope, so compliance and latency are both big.
[00:00:18] Samantha: Totally. Quick agenda: Carlos will demo Optimize console, we'll build a precision profile for your demo workload, then discuss deployment options and pilot next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:27] Tom: Yup. Also want to validate that rollback story — we can't have hallucinations hitting clinicians.
[00:00:32] Carlos: Absolutely. I'll start with the sandbox so you can see live heatmaps. One note — transcript might show some mis-words; the console labels sometimes render as K-V "cash" in the transcript.
[00:00:42] Samantha: ha, yeah. K-V cache.
[00:00:45] [00:01:02] Carlos: (screen share) ok starting the Optimize console. Top-left is model catalog, we're using an open 8B family snapshot here. In the profiles tab you can see the default precision policy — mix of FP16 for embedding prep and FP32 fallback for long-form gen. We'll create a new profile named "mediscribe-triage-int8fp8".
[00:01:22] Tom: question — will that profile be portable to Dedicated/private? We want to run in VPC later.
[00:01:27] Carlos: Yes, profiles are metadata stored in your control plane and can be exported. Private deployments support the same profile schema; only the runtime quant kernels change slightly based on hardware.
[00:01:36] [00:02:10] Carlos: I'm toggling the quant bucket to allow both INT8 (per-channel) and FP8 for attention weights. The optimization suggests an initial guardrail of keeping layernorms at FP16, and automatically marks 2nd half transformer blocks as candidate-INT8.
[00:02:25] Dr. Anika: Is that automatic suggestion based on token length distribution?
[00:02:29] Carlos: Exactly. We feed your sample prompt set and runtime characteristics, and Optimize proposes bitwidths. For example, short prompts with 32-64 tokens will favor INT8 for throughput; long notes hitting 512+ tokens push toward FP8 to preserve fidelity.
[00:02:45] [00:03:05] Carlos: I'm running an on-the-fly fidelity sweep. See the heatmap — x-axis is sequence length buckets, y-axis is precision profile. The color indicates Delta-BLEU-like fidelity drop relative to FP16 baseline. Right now INT8 shows a 2-3% drop for 64 tokens but 8-12% at 1024 tokens for instruction-following.
[00:03:25] Tom: that delta sounds significant for our clinical summarization. What metric are you using for fidelity?
[00:03:31] Carlos: Good call — it's a composite we call Q-score: mix of ROUGE-L, factuality ratio (from our eval harness) and clinician-labeled critical error rate. We weight factuality highest. I can share the eval config.
[00:03:42] [00:04:10] Priya: important to note: you can pin on critical prompt sets to force FP8 or FP16 for certain routes. So you'd get INT8 throughput for quick triage but FP8/FP16 for sections flagged as high-risk.
[00:04:18] Ravi: And runtime cost delta between INT8 and FP8?
[00:04:22] Carlos: In our benchmarks INT8 gave ~1.8-2.5x token throughput improvement and ~40-55% cost reduction on GPU runtime compared to FP16 for typical batch sizes. FP8 sits in between — around 1.3-1.6x and 20-35% cost reduction, but with much smaller fidelity loss on long form.
[00:04:41] [00:05:00] Samantha: Also mention autoscaling impacts — latency budgets interact with batching. If you set a strict p95 latency target, Optimize may reduce batch sizes which erodes INT8 throughput gains.
[00:05:08] Tom: So there's a tradeoff — we can't sacrify too much fidelity. We need tail latency under 250ms for triage. Is that feasible with INT8?
[00:05:16] Carlos: For short responses yes, at small batch sizes INT8 can meet 250ms p95. But worst-case for 512+ tokens you'll hit >500ms unless you scale out capacity. That's where Dedicated pools and burst capacity help.
[00:05:30] [00:06:10] Dr. Anika: About data-in-flight and at-rest — we need KMS. We have an internal HSM. How does Redwood integrate?
[00:06:17] Samantha: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM via standard KMS APIs; for Private on-prem deployments we can integrate with your HSM using the Redwood agent. We'll share the security pack.
[00:06:25] Lena: And audit logs? We need per-request audit logs for compliance and retention controls.
[00:06:29] Carlos: Console has request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns. In Private mode logs can be stored in your S3 and forwarded to your SIEM. There is a small overhead but it's optional.
[00:06:40] [00:07:05] Carlos: Back to the profile — I'm adding a fallback rule: if predicted quality for a prompt is below threshold, route to FP8 for the first pass; if still below, route to a local FP16 fallback. Fallbacks can be timebound to avoid double-cost for all requests.
[00:07:18] Tom: How do you predict quality? Is it an on-device classifier?
[00:07:21] Carlos: We use a lightweight predictor trained on your eval set — it runs in the control plane and uses prompt-level signals (length, entity density) to estimate expected Q-score. It's probabilistic so we allow conservative thresholds.
[00:07:35] [00:08:02] Samantha: Quick pause — any blockers you're thinking of?
[00:08:05] Dr. Anika: The big one is pilot scope. We want a pilot that includes PHI but only in a private VPC. So we'd need private deployment or maybe dedicated with strict egress rules.
[00:08:16] Samantha: Understood — we can do Dedicated for isolated GPU pools with VPC peering, or Private (customer-managed control plane). Both support our precision profiles. For PHI, we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with a strict contract.
[00:08:30] [00:08:45] Carlos: I'm now running a latency profile for your sample workload. The console shows p50/p95/p99 lines as we sweep batch sizes and quant profiles. See p95 for INT8 at batch 1 is 210ms for 64 tokens, p95 for FP8 is 270ms.
[00:08:59] Tom: ok that's close. Will there be artifacts where INT8 introduces wrong entities?
[00:09:05] Carlos: Yes, INT8 occasionally drops specificity like medication dosages in long completions. That's why we recommend hybrid profiles: INT8 for opening summaries, FP8 for sections with numeric or temporal entities.
[00:09:18] [00:09:40] Priya: We also have canary rollout helpers — you can route 5% of traffic to INT8 and compare Q-score in real time, with automatic rollback if error budget exceeded.
[00:09:50] Ravi: latency SLOs for clinician-facing vs internal triage differ. Can we tie routes to RBAC?
[00:09:55] Carlos: Yes RBAC at route level; you can map API keys to route definitions and policies.
[00:10:05] [00:10:30] Carlos: Running a quality visualization — here's a time-series that overlays Q-score and cost per 1k tokens. Notice when we move from FP8 to INT8 cost dips but occasionally a Q-score blip. We can set automated alerts when Q-score drops beyond X points.
[00:10:51] Dr. Anika: How noisy are those alerts? We need to avoid pager fatigue.
[00:10:55] Samantha: You can tune alert windows and only surface high-confidence regressions. Also we can send aggregated daily digests and let SREs decide.
[00:11:08] [00:11:30] Carlos: Quick demo of profile export — I'm exporting the med-profile JSON. This contains the precision map, fallback rules, guardrails, and the eval hooks. You'll get this and you can import into a Dedicated or Private control plane.
[00:11:46] Tom: Any compatibility issues with GPUs like A100 vs H100 or AWS G5?
[00:11:51] Carlos: Kernels differ; we auto-select best kernels per hardware. INT8 performance on A100 vs H100 may vary — H100 has better tensor core FP8 paths. Optimize will flag recommended profile per hardware.
[00:12:05] [00:12:40] Carlos: Running an adversarial check — I fed in a long clinical note designed to stress numerical fidelity. See the regression — INT8 loses dose specificity. The console recommends a per-prompt override to force FP8 when numeric entity density > 0.2.
[00:12:55] Dr. Anika: That detection — is it deterministic? If it misses, we might get false negatives.
[00:12:59] Carlos: It's heuristic plus ML scorer. You can tune thresholds and include whitelist prompts that always use FP16.
[00:13:15] [00:13:35] Samantha: Let's talk pilot numbers — you mentioned 1M tokens/week, right?
[00:13:39] Tom: yeah, around that for initial pilot. Latency target p95 250ms for triage summaries, and critical-case p95 under 500ms with FP8 fallback.
[00:13:50] Samantha: Good. For that footprint, we can start with a small Dedicated pool or private sandbox cluster. Carlos will run a sandbox benchmark to estimate cost and tail latency.
[00:13:59] [00:14:20] Carlos: On the benchmarks, I'll run three profiles: pure FP16 baseline, FP8 hybrid, and INT8 aggressive. I'll measure p50/p95/p99, cost/1k tokens, and Q-score on your eval set.
[00:14:30] Ravi: For the private option, what are the onboarding timelines?
[00:14:34] Samantha: Private can be 4-8 weeks depending on network and security reviews; Dedicated can be faster — typically 2-3 weeks to provision with committed capacity.
[00:14:44] [00:15:05] Lena: Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs? Also do you support SAML SSO?
[00:15:10] Priya: Yes SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001. SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[00:15:18] Lena: Great. Also need data retention policy for logs and how long token-level traces are kept.
[00:15:24] Carlos: By default 30 days but configurable — Private modes can set any retention you want subject to storage.
[00:15:30] [00:16:00] Carlos: Switching to an examples mode — here's a side-by-side: INT8 output vs FP8 for the same prompt. INT8 is faster but you can see missing temporal qualifiers and a dropped medication frequency.
[00:16:13] Tom: I'd like an automated diff that highlights dropped entities so we can triage.
[00:16:18] Carlos: We have an eval diff tool that flags missing entity and hallucination deltas. I'll include that report with the benchmark.
[00:16:33] [00:17:05] Samantha: We're at about 45% through time. Any other big constraints we didn't ask?
[00:17:11] Dr. Anika: Budget is tight. We need cost-saving levers but also must not increase manual review load.
[00:17:16] Samantha: The hybrid profile strategy is designed exactly for that — get cost savings for the bulk and keep high-fidelity paths for risky items.
[00:17:22] [00:17:45] Carlos: Now demonstrating the canary workflow — create a canary route at 10%. The console compares baseline FP16 vs candidate INT8 in real time, with traffic shadowing. If critical-error-rate increases beyond 0.5% we auto-roll back.
[00:17:59] Ravi: Shadowing doubles compute, correct?
[00:18:02] Carlos: Shadowing can be configured in two modes: full shadow (exec duplicates) or sampling-only (only score differences without full execution) — sampling reduces compute overhead.
[00:18:14] [00:18:40] Tom: About the eval hooks — can we plug in our internal deterministic checkers?
[00:18:44] Carlos: Yes, the eval hooks are extensible; you can upload custom checkers that run post-gen and report metrics to the console. We'll provide the API spec.
[00:18:59] [00:19:22] Priya: Another operational note: prefix caching and KV cache can help for repeated substring completions — but caches interplay with precision and may require cache invalidation on profile change.
[00:19:33] Tom: Good to know. We sometimes have repeat templates.
[00:19:40] [00:20:05] Carlos: I'm exporting the profile and the suggested rollout playbook. Playbook includes canary at 5%, 30min observation windows, alert on Q-drop > 1.5 points, and automatic 30% fallback threshold.
[00:20:19] Dr. Anika: One more question — in private mode, do you still run the model compilation stage on Redwood infra or is that local?
[00:20:25] Carlos: For Private on-prem we provide a compilation artifact that you can run locally; for Private with managed nodes we can compile on-prem as part of provisioning given your hardware profile.
[00:20:38] [00:21:02] Samantha: Ok quick recap: Redwood will share sandbox invite and profile export; Carlos will run three benchmarks and the diff; Mediscribe to confirm pilot scope and requirements (KMS/HSM, VPC). Schedule security deep-dive next week.
[00:21:19] Dr. Anika: Sounds good. Any pricing estimate now or after benchmark?
[00:21:24] Samantha: We'll send a ballpark for Dedicated vs Private based on your 1M tokens/week, but final pricing after the benchmark.
[00:21:33] Tom: Also want the rollback runbook; we need to see human-in-the-loop escalation steps.
[00:21:38] Carlos: We'll include a written rollback runbook and the canary configuration in the export.
[00:21:45] [00:22:10] Samantha: Alright let's capture next steps — I'll follow up with the sandbox link and security pack. Carlos will own the benchmarks.
[00:22:17] Ravi: thanks, this was helpful.
[00:22:20] Samantha: Thanks everyone. We'll send minutes + action items.

(End of recording)
